blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — tamoxifen uterine malignancy warning and gynecologic symptom teaching
stem: A client taking tamoxifen asks which gynecologic symptom should be reported promptly for evaluation. Which response by the nurse is best?

options.A: Report abnormal vaginal bleeding, changes in vaginal discharge, menstrual irregularities, or new pelvic pain or pressure promptly for evaluation.
options.B: Gynecologic symptoms are concerning mainly after tamoxifen is discontinued, so bleeding or discharge during active therapy can usually wait until routine follow-up.
options.C: Tamoxifen does not require special attention to vaginal bleeding or other gynecologic symptoms because uterine malignancy risk is not increased with treatment.
options.D: Routine endometrial biopsy should replace symptom-triggered evaluation in asymptomatic clients because scheduled sampling is recommended throughout tamoxifen therapy.

rationale: Current tamoxifen labeling reports an increased incidence of uterine malignancies, including endometrial adenocarcinoma and uterine sarcoma. It states that any patient receiving or who has previously received tamoxifen who reports abnormal vaginal bleeding should be promptly evaluated and advises prompt reporting of other abnormal gynecologic symptoms such as menstrual irregularities, changes in vaginal discharge, or pelvic pain or pressure. The label also states that routine endometrial sampling in asymptomatic women has not been shown beneficial. Therefore A is correct. B improperly delays evaluation, C denies the warning, and D substitutes unsupported routine sampling for symptom-triggered evaluation.
educational_objective: Teach clients receiving or previously exposed to tamoxifen to promptly report abnormal vaginal bleeding and other abnormal gynecologic symptoms because uterine malignancies are a recognized risk requiring evaluation.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_version_date: Current DailyMed labeling dated December 18, 2025 and verified 2026-08-26
source_locator: Warnings — Effects on the Uterus / Endometrial Cancer and Uterine Sarcoma: increased uterine malignancies; promptly evaluate abnormal vaginal bleeding in current or previous users; advise prompt reporting of abnormal gynecologic symptoms; routine endometrial sampling in asymptomatic women has no demonstrated benefit.
source_claim_supported: Tamoxifen is associated with increased uterine malignancies; abnormal vaginal bleeding and other abnormal gynecologic symptoms during or after treatment warrant prompt evaluation, while routine endometrial sampling of asymptomatic women is not supported.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: educate clients about medications; identify adverse effects; monitor/evaluate medication therapy.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as complete gynecologic-monitoring statements without absolute-word distractor cues.
Used current DailyMed uterine-warning language and explicitly distinguished symptom-triggered evaluation from unsupported routine endometrial sampling.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely follows current tamoxifen labeling. B delays required evaluation, C denies uterine risk, and D recommends unsupported routine sampling; no second defensible answer remains.
